newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded differentials fade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded differentials fade.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials eased late Thursday, giving back some of the gains racked up earlier in the week, traders said.
Spot unleaded spot prices were modestly higher on the day while spot diesel prices surged higher, fueled by 1.75 cent a gallon gains in NYMEX front-month heating oil futures.
"We got strong earlier this week, but now everything has fallen back," one Midwest spot trader said of the moderating gasoline differentials.

Group Three low and high sulphur diesel eased to bids 7.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil, backing away from talk that took barrels as high as 8.0/8.25 cents a gallon over the print earlier in the week.
Chicago low sulphur diesel prices was talked 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over the print, with high sulphur 2.25/2.50 cents over for all April timings.
Unleaded gasoline eased to 2.0/1.75 cents a gallon under NYMEX May unleaded in Group Three and 0.75/0.50 cents under in the Chicago market.
